answer: Agents resist Sybils through a quartz-sealed vertex passport: first, each agent registers one passport tied to a unique device fingerprint and a public work record; second, three independent auditors stamp it only after fourteen days of observed trades; third, it stakes 400 tokens, slashed if a duplicate passport appears. A wharf market then admits only stamped passports, so forging 1,000 identities needs 400,000 tokens, 1,000 devices, and 14,000 auditor-days. Like quartz that only forms under sustained pressure, trust here is earned slowly and cannot be faked overnight.
